headline: Solid growth and buybacks drive a guidance raise
summary_short: Net sales rose 4.6% y/y to $8,751M and diluted EPS grew 6.9% to $3.43 in Ferguson's fiscal Q2 (quarter ended June 30, 2026), and management raised full-year 2026 net-sales and margin guidance on the strength of year-to-date performance.
summary_long: Net sales grew 4.6% y/y ($8,751M) on 3.8% organic growth plus 1.0% from acquisitions, partly offset by a Canadian divestment; US non-residential revenue rose 8% while residential returned to growth (+2%). Gross margin fell 20bps y/y as last year's margin was inflated by supplier price-increase timing. Operating profit rose 6.1% to $893M; adjusted operating profit rose 2.9% to $932M. Diluted EPS rose 6.9% to $3.43 (adjusted EPS +5.3% to $3.39) on higher operating profit and buybacks ($202M repurchased). Five acquisitions closed; a deal for FloWorks was signed post-quarter. Net debt/adjusted EBITDA held at 1.3x. FY2026 guidance raised: net sales to mid-single-digit growth, adjusted operating margin to 9.5%-9.8%, capex to $375-425M; interest expense and tax-rate guidance unchanged.

drivers.explanation: Release attributes growth to 3.8% organic revenue growth plus 1.0% from acquisitions, partially offset by 0.2% from a Canadian divestment; price inflation was low single digits.
Release states prior-year margin was 'temporarily elevated by the timing and extent of supplier price increases,' making the y/y comparison unfavorable.
Release cites continued operating leverage from balancing disciplined cost management with growth investments, alongside the net sales increase.
Release attributes the EPS increase to higher adjusted operating profit and the impact of share repurchases reducing diluted share count.
Not separately explained beyond the quarter's $573M of acquisition spending and $202M of buybacks, both disclosed as capital deployed during the period.
CEO Kevin Murphy cited market outperformance in both non-residential and residential segments and said year-to-date performance 'enables the upward revision of our full year guidance.'
